item.title: Effective JavaScript Techniques for Detecting Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge Versions
item.description:
“Effective JavaScript Techniques for Detecting Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge Versions”

Determining the specific browser, especially legacy versions like Internet Explorer (IE) or discerning modern Edge versions, is often required for compatibility shims or feature flagging. Since user agent (UA) strings have evolved significantly—particularly with Edge adopting the Chromium engine—the detection logic needs refinement.

What are the most effective strategies for detecting different versions of Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge using client-side JavaScript, avoiding deprecated methods where possible?

item.title: JavaScript Client Browser Detection Methods Via Navigator UserAgent
item.description:
“JavaScript Client Browser Detection Methods Via Navigator UserAgent”

How can a developer reliably determine the client’s browser name and version within a web application using JavaScript, given the inconsistencies and obfuscation in the navigator.userAgent string across different browsers, especially modern ones like Edge and IE11?

Developers often need this information for applying specific compatibility fixes, sorting error reports, or tailoring UI experiences. Relying solely on navigator.appName or navigator.appVersion frequently yields generic or misleading results. We examine several accepted strategies for more precise client environment introspection.
